reason: I'd install it because the batch convert and the screenshot importer sound handy, but it's 0.4.1 from one person and I don't want my default viewer to be a risk. ImageGlass stays as default until I've seen NuViewer behave for a while.
why_switch_or_not: The feature list is tempting for me: gallery, batch rename/convert, a simple editor and ICC colour management in one free app, plus the speed numbers for flipping through lots of PNGs. But I'd only try it on a copy of a screenshot folder first. I would not make it default until I know it doesn't touch my colour handling, and I don't know how it treats the sidecar edit file or any metadata. I also don't want to tick all the formats in Windows Settings by hand for something I might drop in two weeks.
current_app_pros: ImageGlass looks modern and clean, is open source, and opens my PNG screenshots and PDFs without any fuss. I know where everything is and the file associations are already set.
current_app_pains: It can feel a bit slow when I hold the arrow key through a few hundred screenshots, and it doesn't do batch convert or real editing, so I end up opening another tool for that.
objection: My colour management and file workflow must not change, and it's a single developer on version 0.4.1. I can't tell if my files and metadata stay exactly as they are, or whether it will still be maintained in a year.
would_change_my_mind: A clear statement that it never modifies originals or metadata unless I save, and that colour handling matches what I have now. A few months of regular releases would also help, or someone I trust saying they use it daily.
